item.title: Global tourism reaches record 1.52 billion as Finland sets overnight stay record
item.description: International tourism reached a new record in 2025, with 1.52 billion people travelling abroad, according to the latest World Tourism Barometer from UN Tourism. The figure marks a 4 per cent increase on 2024 and stands almost 60 million above the previous peak recorded in 2019 before the pandemic. Europe remained the largest destination region, attracting 793 million international arrivals.

item.title: Trump sets global tariffs to 15 per cent after Supreme Court ruling
item.description: US President Donald Trump has raised global import tariffs to 15 per cent days after the Supreme Court ruled that his earlier levies broke the law. The move deepens a dispute between the White House and the court and leaves businesses seeking refunds for an estimated $133bn collected under the previous regime. On Friday, the Supreme Court held that Trump had exceeded his authority by imposing broad tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act of 1977.

item.title: Helsinki orders 20,000 euro fine for Alanya Market over labelling breaches
item.description: Helsinki has imposed a 20,000 euro conditional fine on Armina Oy, the company that operates Alanya Market in the Itis shopping centre, after inspectors found missing Finnish and Swedish labelling on dozens of food products. Helsingin Uutiset first reported the fine. The decision follows an inspection that revealed breaches of European Union rules on packaging information. The city’s environment and permits sub-committee approved the fine at a meeting on Thursday 13 February.

item.title: Finland win Olympic bronze in ice hockey with 6–1 victory over Slovakia
item.description: Finland secured Olympic bronze in men’s ice hockey with a 6–1 victory over Slovakia in Saturday’s medal match, sealing the country’s eighth Olympic medal in the sport. The win marked Finland’s fifth bronze and continued a run of podium finishes in tournaments featuring NHL players. In six such Olympic events, Finland have claimed five medals. item.title: Russia launches mass strikes across Ukraine, Lviv blast kills officer
item.description: Russia fired 50 missiles and 297 drones at Ukraine overnight, targeting Kyiv and energy facilities across the country, Ukrainian officials said on Sunday. Air defences shot down 33 missiles and 274 drones, the air force reported. At least one person died in the Kyiv region. Explosions also killed a 23-year-old police officer in Lviv after devices detonated when officers responded to a call. item.title: USA win men’s Olympic ice hockey gold
item.description: Team USA claimed the Olympic men’s ice hockey title on Sunday with a 2-1 overtime victory over Canada in Milan, sealing the country’s first gold medal in the event since 1980. Jack Hughes scored the decisive goal 1:41 into sudden death overtime. Zach Werenski carried the puck out of defence and fed Hughes, who beat Canada goaltender Jordan Binnington from close range to end the contest. The United States last won Olympic gold in men’s hockey at Lake Placid in 1980.

item.title: New strike wave set for private care sector in Finland
item.description: Finland’s private social services sector faces a new three-day strike in March after two major unions issued fresh notices amid a protracted pay dispute. The action will run from 10 to 12 March and follows a walkout last week that affected care homes in the north of the country. Talks under the national conciliator continue without a settlement. item.title: Court remands 32-year-old father over suspected attempt on baby’s life
item.description: A district court in Oulu has remanded a 32-year-old man on suspicion of attempting to kill his two-week-old son and assaulting the child’s mother. The decision followed a custody hearing on Monday. Prosecutors must file charges by 7 May. Police allege that the man assaulted his partner and then threw the infant onto a concrete floor in a stairwell of an apartment building near central Oulu in the early hours of Friday.

item.title: EU halts approval of US trade deal after court ruling on Trump tariffs
item.description: The European Union will delay ratification of its trade agreement with the United States after the US Supreme Court struck down a large share of tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump. The decision follows a ruling on Friday that found Trump lacked authority to introduce several duties last spring. After the judgment, Trump announced new across-the-board import tariffs of 10 per cent. The rate rose to 15 per cent on Saturday.

item.title: Finnish quantum firm IQM to list in New York at 1.8bn dollars
item.description: Finnish quantum computing company IQM will list on the New York Stock Exchange through a merger with a special purpose acquisition company, valuing the business at 1.8 billion dollars. The Espoo-based group will combine with the listed SPAC Real Asset Acquisition Corp. The transaction gives IQM access to US public markets. The deal requires approval from shareholders and regulators before completion. The valuation equals about 1.5 to 1.6 billion euros, according to figures released on Monday.
